directions: Plant bulbs 2-3 inches deep in well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade in late summer. Autumn Snowflake is a diminutive fall-blooming bulb, sending up thread-like stems bearing one or two small, nodding, bell-shaped white flowers delicately flushed with pink at the base, often appearing before or alongside the grassy foliage in late summer to early fall — a welcome bit of bloom when little else in the bulb garden is active. It is smaller and daintier than its better-known spring and summer snowflake relatives, and unlike those moisture-loving cousins it actually prefers a drier summer rest, making it well suited to a sunny, well-drained border or rock garden rather than a damp woodland setting. Once established it slowly multiplies by offset bulbs and self-seeding, and like many old Southern pass-along bulbs it needs no supplemental water or feeding to keep returning each fall for years.
